title: Park ends Sun Yang's run at WTT Star Contender Muscat as Odo wins four times and takes doubles title
seo_title: WTT Star Contender Muscat day 5: Park ends Sun Yang run
description: WTT Star Contender Muscat day five: Park Ganghyeon beat Sun Yang, Akae came from 2-0 down, Odo and Yokoi won the women's doubles and Lim and Oh the men's.
standfirst: Satsuki Odo won all four of her matches on Friday, Honoka Hashimoto and Shunsuke Togami went through without dropping a game, and Kaho Akae set up an all-Japanese semi-final.

body: Sun Yang's run at WTT Star Contender Muscat ended in the last 16 on Friday, when South Korea's Park Ganghyeon beat the 18-year-old Chinese defender 11-5 in the fifth game. Satsuki Odo won all four of her matches on the busiest day of the week, taking the women's doubles title with Sakura Yokoi and reaching the singles semi-finals, while Honoka Hashimoto and Shunsuke Togami, the second seeds, went through without dropping a game.

Kaho Akae, the 12th seed, came from two games down to beat Miyu Nagasaki 13-11 in the fifth and set up an all-Japanese semi-final against Odo. South Korea's Lim Jonghoon and Oh Junsung, who had played each other in the singles that morning, won the men's doubles title against India's Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah.
## Park ends Sun's run

Sun, ranked 228th, had won five matches in four days, the last of them a 3-1 win over the top seed Darko Jorgic, as Eleven's [day four review](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-day-four-review-results-highlights.html) described. Sun took the fourth game 14-12 to level at 2-2, but Park, 30 and the world No 44, pulled away in the decider. It took 38 minutes.

Park then beat France's Flavien Coton, the eighth seed and at 18 the youngest player left in the men's draw, 11-8 in the fifth game of their quarter-final. Coton had won the second game 11-2 and the fourth 11-9. Park plays his compatriot Oh in the semi-finals: Oh, 20 and the fifth seed, beat Lim 16-14, 11-8, 14-16, 5-11, 11-7 in the last 16 and then swept Russia's Vladimir Sidorenko, the fourth seed, 11-9, 11-9, 11-6.
## Togami and Hashimoto drop nothing

Togami, the world No 15, lost the first game to France's Joe Seyfried and then conceded nine points in the next three. In the quarter-finals he beat Dimitrij Ovtcharov 12-10, 11-9, 15-13 in 28 minutes. Ovtcharov, 38, had beaten South Korea's 18-year-old qualifier Kwon Hyuk 3-0 in the morning.

Hashimoto, the Japanese defender who won [WTT Contender Istanbul](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html) last Sunday, conceded 14 points in beating South Korea's Kim Seongjin 11-1, 11-7, 11-6 and 15 in beating Taiwan's Cheng I-Ching, the 10th seed, 11-7, 11-3, 11-5. She has now won eight matches in a row on the WTT tour. Cheng had beaten Yokoi, the sixth seed, 3-0 in the last 16.
## Akae's comeback and the women's semi-finals

Nagasaki, the fourth seed and the world No 18, won the first two games 11-9 and 11-7. Akae, 22 and ranked 36th, then won the third 11-3 and the fourth 11-2, and took the decider 13-11 after 34 minutes. She had beaten China's Qin Yuxuan, the seventh seed, 11-6, 11-2, 11-3 in the last 16.

Odo, the top seed, beat France's Audrey Zarif 3-0 and then South Korea's Kim Nayeong 11-5, 11-6, 11-6 in 18 minutes, the quickest quarter-final of the day. Kim had needed 49 minutes and a 14-12 fifth game to beat Russia's Elizabet Abraamian, who led 2-0.

The other semi-final is between Hashimoto and Romania's Bernadette Szőcs, the fifth seed, who beat Japan's Sachi Aoki 3-0 and then South Korea's Joo Cheonhui, the third seed, 11-8, 12-10, 7-11, 11-7. Joo had played the longest match of the day in the last 16, 58 minutes, before beating China's Wang Xiaotong 11-9 in the fifth game.
## China's last man standing

Chen Yuanyu, 21, is China's only player left in either singles draw. He beat the qualifier Yuan Licen 3-11, 11-8, 7-11, 11-6, 11-5 in an all-Chinese quarter-final, a day after Yuan had knocked out the 19-year-old defender Li Tianyang 12-10 in the fifth game. Chen's last-16 win over Japan's Hiroto Shinozuka, the sixth seed, is recorded in WTT's official result as 11-9, 11-7, 11-0, with no match time given; Rallys later reported that Shinozuka retired during the match, and five days later he withdrew from Japan's Mixed Team World Cup squad. Chen meets Togami in the semi-finals.
## Doubles titles for Japan and South Korea

Odo and Yokoi, the second seeds, scored the first five points of the women's doubles final and beat the top seeds Kim Nayeong and Joo 11-7, 11-9, 11-6 in 26 minutes. Lim and Oh lost the first game of the men's final 12-10 to Thakkar and Shah, then won the next three 11-2, 11-8, 11-8.

Odo is still in two more finals. She and Togami beat Australia's Nicholas Lum and Yangzi Liu 11-5, 6-11, 12-10, 12-10 in the mixed doubles semi-finals and play France's Esteban Dorr and Jia Nan Yuan, who beat Romania's Eduard Ionescu and Szőcs 3-1, in Saturday's final.

## Saturday: semi-finals and finals

The semi-finals start at 7am UK time (11am in Muscat) with Odo against Akae, followed by Chen against Togami at 7.40am, Szőcs against Hashimoto at 8.20am and Park against Oh at 9am. The mixed doubles final is at 9.30am, the women's singles final at 1.30pm and the men's at 2.10pm. Singles matches become best of seven games from the semi-finals. The full order of play is in Eleven's [finals day preview](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-day-six-preview-order-of-play.html).
